Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Message
The Labour manifesto presents a vision of "change" after 14 years of Conservative government, promising to end what it characterises as chaos, restore hope, and rebuild Britain through mission-driven governance focused on serving working people.

## Five National Missions

**1. Kickstart Economic Growth**
Labour pledges to achieve the highest sustained growth in the G7 through a new industrial strategy, a National Wealth Fund capitalised with £7.3 billion to attract private investment, planning reform to build 1.5 million homes, and devolution of powers to local leaders. The party commits to capping corporation tax at 25% and reforming business rates.

**2. Clean Energy Superpower**
The manifesto promises clean electricity by 2030 through Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, capitalised with £8.3 billion. Plans include doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind, alongside a £6.6 billion Warm Homes Plan to upgrade five million homes.

**3. Take Back Our Streets**
Labour aims to halve serious violent crime and violence against women and girls within a decade. This includes recruiting thousands of neighbourhood police officers, introducing Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour, specialist rape units in every police force, and a youth intervention programme.

**4. Break Down Barriers to Opportunity**
Educational reforms include recruiting 6,500 new teachers funded by ending private school tax exemptions, 3,000 new primary school nurseries, free breakfast clubs, curriculum review, and a Skills England body. Labour commits to a Youth Guarantee for 18-21 year-olds.

**5. NHS Fit for the Future**
The party pledges 40,000 extra weekly appointments, 8,500 additional mental health staff, doubling cancer scanners, a dentistry rescue plan, and social care reform towards a National Care Service.

## Foundational Commitments

**Economic Stability**: Strict fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day spending and falling debt by the fifth forecast year. No increases to income tax, National Insurance, or VAT.

**National Security**: Unwavering NATO commitment, maintaining the nuclear deterrent, a Strategic Defence Review, and steadfast Ukraine support.

**Border Security**: A new Border Security Command replacing the Rwanda scheme, additional caseworkers to clear asylum backlogs, and ending asylum hotels.

## Funding Mechanisms
Revenue comes from abolishing non-dom tax status, closing carried interest loopholes, extending and strengthening the windfall tax on oil and gas companies, VAT on private schools, and tackling tax avoidance.

## Constitutional Reform
Proposals include removing hereditary peers, introducing mandatory retirement at 80 for Lords, votes at 16, an Ethics and Integrity Commission, and improved relations with devolved governments through a Council of the Nations and Regions.

## International Outlook
Labour promises to rebuild European relationships without rejoining the EU, seek a UK-EU security pact, champion climate leadership through a Clean Power Alliance, and restore 0.7% development spending when fiscally possible.

# Summary: Conservative Party Manifesto 2024

## Economic Stability and Growth

The Conservative manifesto positions the party as guardians of economic stability following pandemic and Ukraine crisis challenges. With inflation reduced, real wages rising, and growth returning, the Conservatives pledge to continue their economic plan by cutting National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, saving average workers £1,350. Self-employed individuals would see their main rate of National Insurance abolished entirely. The party commits to maintaining fiscal rules, reducing debt, backing businesses through competitive taxation, and investing in infrastructure—including £36 billion in transport projects from HS2 savings.

## Immigration and Border Security

A central pledge involves introducing a legal, binding cap on migration that falls annually, with parliamentary oversight. The party promises to continue Rwanda deportation flights for illegal migrants, crack down on organised immigration crime, and reform international asylum rules. Work visa thresholds have been increased to £38,700, and family visa income requirements will rise with inflation.

## Defence and National Security

Defence spending will increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, representing the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The manifesto emphasises support for Ukraine, modernisation of armed forces, investment in nuclear deterrence, and strengthened veteran support including a new Veterans' Bill.

## Public Services

NHS spending will rise above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Mental health support will expand, including 100% coverage of Mental Health Support Teams in schools by 2030. Social care reform continues with cost-capping from October 2025.

## Housing and Communities

The Conservatives target 1.6 million new homes, abolishing legacy EU nutrient neutrality rules to unlock 100,000 homes immediately. Stamp Duty abolition continues for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000, alongside a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Environment and Energy

While maintaining commitment to net zero by 2050, the party takes a "pragmatic approach," promising no new green levies, annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, and trebling offshore wind capacity. Nuclear expansion through Small Modular Reactors is prioritised.

## Family Support and Young People

Working parents receive 30 hours free childcare from nine months old. Child Benefit moves to household assessment, benefiting families until combined income reaches £120,000. National Service becomes mandatory for 18-year-olds, offering military or civic service options.
